_: What each skill and penalty is called (P3-76, Q169, the user's ask): the
items of the driving test's fault sheet, TD 553, the 黃紙 every Hong Kong
driver took home from the test. Read by scripts/fares/exam_sheet.gd for
FareFace.skill_name — the flash under the clock and the receipt — and held
by tools/verify_hud.gd in both languages. JSON beside menu_text.json, which
hard rule 4 permits: these are words, not tuning.
The NAMES only (the user's call): a bonus is still a bonus and a penalty a
penalty, and TD's own rule that three minor faults on one item make a
serious one is NOT applied. The tier word is what tells two events on the
same item apart — a near miss from a close call, a bump from a crash.
Sourced: TD's Guide to Private Car and Light Goods Vehicle Driving Test
(Nov 2025, both languages) for 輕微 / 嚴重 and Minor / Serious. The item
wording is the 黃紙's as driving schools quote it — the form itself is not
published — and its English is ours: TD's English names for the items are
unverified. 早到 is the passenger's, not the examiner's, and keeps its name.
甩尾 keeps its name too (the user's call): the sheet's 軚盤控制不當 opens
with 軚 (U+8EDA), which Free HK Kai does not carry, and the web build has
no system face to fall back on.
Keys are Fare.Skill's names, lower-cased: an entry per value, so a skill
appended to the enum without a name here fails verify_hud.
